remediated_by: OpenCode CLI (Together . GLM-5.3 Flash High), remediator r1

findings.title: `remember --dry-run` and `admit --file` text-mode views misrender results and violate preview contract
findings.evidence: crates/clio-lib/src/cli_write_core.rs:80-86,263-295; executing `clio remember "test" --category persona --dry-run --output text` outputs `stored ? (admission_score 0.7100000000000001)` falsely indicating mutation; executing `clio admit --file ops.json --output text` outputs a bare `preview` string omitting batch summary counts (`would_admit`, `would_reject`, `writes`)
findings.requirement_ref: phase-100370 §1 Expected Outcome ("`clio remember --dry-run` and `clio admit ...` print score and factors without writing"), §5 Task 1, §8 (T100370-02), AC-100370-02, gaps/full-cli.md §6
findings.recommendation: In `CoreWriteGroup::render` (`crates/clio-lib/src/cli_write_core.rs`), inspect the payload: if `payload.get("dry_run") == Some(&Value::Bool(true))` or `verb == "admit"`, route to `render_preview(payload)` rather than `render_stored(payload)`. In `render_preview`, handle batch preview payloads (when `summary` or `count` is present, render `preview: {count} items (would_admit: {would_admit}, would_reject: {would_reject})`). Add unit tests in `cli_write_core_tests.rs` for both text-mode outputs.
findings.resolution: Fixed in crates/clio-lib/src/cli_write_core.rs. `CoreWriteGroup::render` now routes a `remember` payload with `dry_run: true` to `render_preview` (routing on `dry_run` only, because a real `store` success payload also carries `pass`/`admission_score`, so routing on `pass` would misclassify real writes); `admit` payloads with `summary`/`count` route to the new `render_batch_preview`, which prints `preview: {count} items (would_admit: N, would_reject: N, writes: N)` with deterministic zero fallbacks. Added 2 end-to-end text-mode tests (`text_mode_remember_dry_run_renders_the_preview_not_a_write`, `text_mode_admit_file_renders_the_batch_summary`) and extended `render_views_fall_back_deterministically` with batch cases. Evidence: fixed binary output — `clio remember ... --dry-run --output text` -> `preview: pass / score: 0.7800000000000001 / factors: confidence=0.5 novelty=1.0 recency=1.0 type_prior=0.9 utility=0.5` (exit 0, no `stored` text); `clio admit --file ops.json --output text` -> `preview: 2 items (would_admit: 2, would_reject: 0, writes: 0)` (exit 0). Tests: cargo llvm-cov --package clio 359 passed 0 failed (was 357); cli_write_core.rs per-file lines 96.68% / functions 96.43%. Gates: make check PASS (exit 0); make coverage PASS (coverage-guard 297 files, TOTAL lines 97.96% functions 98.95%, all reported files meet the per-file floor).

plan_unlimited.item: Harmonize dry-run preview contract across all write groups: pass execution context/mode to `WriteGroup::render` so groups have uniform, first-class access to whether an invocation is dry-run, avoiding heuristics on payload fields.
plan_unlimited.disposition: deferred with reasons. Evidence: the payload heuristic is only needed for `remember`, the sole verb whose `--dry-run` remaps to a different tool (`admit_preview`); every other group's dry-run goes through `WriteCall::Preview`, which carries its own prebuilt text and never reaches `render`. Changing the `WriteGroup::render` signature would touch every group implementation for no observable behavior change, and a signature change is a cross-cutting API refactor outside this remediation round's scope (no failing behavior beyond F-01, now fixed and tested). If a future verb remaps tools under dry-run, revisit.

plan_unlimited.item: Introduce an automated golden snapshot test suite across all CLI verbs (both read and write surfaces) in both `--output json` and `--output text` modes to prevent UX drift and ensure consistent rendering.
plan_unlimited.disposition: deferred with reasons. This is a phase-sized feature (~30 verbs x 2 output modes), not a remediation for a reported defect; existing golden tests already cover the highest-risk render paths per group (stored id, preview decision, batch summary, job status) plus deterministic fallbacks. Ordering the full suite here would also collide with the 450-line per-file limit and the no-drive-by-refactor rule. Recommend proposing it as its own roadmap phase.
